title: Umar's Red Sea silk raid of 644: how a tiny attack reshaped Islamic finance
hook: A secret 644 raid on Jeddah flooded early Islam with Byzantine silk, sparking an economic revolution.
description:
A secret 644 raid on Jeddah flooded early Islam with Byzantine silk, sparking an economic revolution. Discover how a tiny naval strike rewrote the financial playbook of an empire.

beats.say: In 644, Umar ibn al-Khattab dispatched a small fleet to the Red Sea, aiming to strike Byzantine ports.
The mission targeted the coastal town of Jeddah, then a quiet fishing village, to cripple trade routes.
Surprisingly, the fleet arrived under a moonlit haze, catching the unsuspecting garrison off guard at dawn.
Umar's commander, al-Qays ibn al-Husayn, ordered a swift raid, seizing the harbor's modest warehouses.
Inside, they uncovered hidden caches of Byzantine silk, a treasure worth more than the entire expedition's cost.
Umar then declared the loot a public fund, distributing silk to impoverished Muslims across Arabia.
The unexpected wealth bolstered his reforms, financing the construction of the first Islamic post-road stations.
Byzantine sources later blamed the raid for a sudden spike in silk prices in Constantinople that year.
Historians now view the 644 raid as the first strategic economic warfare in early Islam.
